# BLO-40805 — env guard: data positions are data, not commands

Change: [BLO-40805](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-40805).

Changed files:

- `src/server/env-guard.ts` — both copies (`classifyAgentShellCommand` and the
  in-pod `ENV_GUARD_SCRIPT`) change identically:
  - `simpleCommandDumps` stops at the first ordinary command word. Assignments,
    flags and pass-through wrappers before it keep a later word in command
    position; every word after it is an argument. Once a wrapper is seen the
    scan runs to the end of the command. The wrappers are the new
    `COMMAND_POSITION_WRAPPERS` list (the shells plus `eval`, `sudo`, `su`,
    `timeout`, `xargs`, `watch`, `env` and similar).
  - A quoted word containing a shell separator is re-lexed as a nested command
    only when the same command contains a listed wrapper, so `eval 'ls; env'`
    is still scanned and `grep -iE 'a|env'` is not.
  - Heredocs are lexed. A quoted delimiter (`<<'EOF'`) makes the body inert, and
    it is dropped. An unquoted one (`<<EOF`) is scanned for substitutions only,
    because the shell interpolates the body but never executes its words.
  - The `/proc/*/environ` scan still runs over every word, before the walk.
- `src/server/env-guard.test.ts` — the shared corpus, run through both copies,
  gains allowed cases for the false positives (quoted heredoc bodies that
  mention `env`, `env` inside a grep/jq/sed argument, `echo env`, a
  `#!/usr/bin/env` shebang) and blocked negative controls for the real block
  (substitutions in an unquoted heredoc body, `eval`/`su -c` payloads, and
  `sudo`/`xargs`/`timeout` wrapping a dump utility).

Why: the guard lexed correctly but treated every word of a simple command as a
possible command, and re-lexed any quoted word with a separator in it. So the
name of a dump utility used as an argument, inside a regex alternation, or in a
heredoc body was blocked even though nothing could run it. Seven reproductions
were measured, including writing a test fixture for this guard. Blocking them
taught agents to reach for encoding workarounds.

No upstream change: the env guard (PEN-1305) is Blockcast-local code in the
vendored adapter, not a carried patch against an upstream adapter release.
